<reason>Side B wins by defining opt-in as a separable yes that can be refused without losing the job, then showing boilerplate either lacks that separability or is opt-in under another name. B neutralizes A's paralysis case with one upfront scoped consent and the human-dub fallback, and distinguishes cloning from colorization or human dubbing because it fabricates attributed new utterances from a biometric model. A repeats the forty-holdout and accessibility claims after they were answered and gives an evasive answer on whether the AI rider can be struck without losing work.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Most decisive was B's pressure-question dilemma and follow-through: if the rider can be refused while keeping the job it is opt-in, and if it cannot it is not meaningful consent. A never squarely escaped that fork.</best_rebuttal>
